_doc: Example .dangeresque/config.json — copy to config.json and edit. engineDefaults stores standing provider pins; worker/review select engines and may override model/effort per phase. Omit review to inherit worker.
_doc_codex: Every scheduled Codex phase is checked against the installed model catalog before dispatch. gpt-5.4 and gpt-5.5 support low/medium/high/xhigh, not max. ultra is rejected because it enables delegation.
_doc_verify: Pre-review verification: dangeresque runs each command in the worktree between the worker exit (post-rebase, post-file-count-normalize) and the review pass. Catches drift between worker prose claims ("yarn build passes") and code reality. Empty `commands` array (default) means no-op; opt in by listing commands. The CLI runs them, NOT the engine — `allowedTools` does not constrain them. Commands run in the worktree with DANGERESQUE_ISSUE + DANGERESQUE_MODE + DANGERESQUE_WORKTREE + DANGERESQUE_ARTIFACT / DANGERESQUE_ARTIFACT_JSON env vars, so a check that audits the worker's own run report (claim lint, citation resolver) can find it without re-deriving the timestamped filename.
_doc_scope: Scope subsystem: project-level opportunistic-fix budget. `enabled` toggles file/line caps (denyGlobs apply unconditionally regardless). `denyGlobs` is the project no-fly list — files matching are demoted to `outside` even if a worker categorized them `extension`; security-sensitive paths cannot be laundered. `maxFiles` caps how many opportunistic drive-by files a worker may bundle in one run; `maxLines` caps total LOC across them. Excess opportunistic files are demoted to `scope_report.outside`, and the reviewer adjudicates. Tighten for stricter projects; relax for greenfield.
_doc_dispatchGate: Pre-worker enforcement gate. Runs BEFORE runWorker for configured modes and refuses to dispatch (exit 2) if any blocking check fails. Independent of reviewer output — this fires at the physical dispatch surface, so consumer policy cannot be bypassed by model verdicts. Absent block = gate off. Malformed config throws at load time (fail closed). --force bypasses only the built-in `requireInvestigateBeforeImplement`; project commands always run and their `on_failure` governs. Commands run in projectRoot with DANGERESQUE_ISSUE + DANGERESQUE_MODE env vars. DANGERESQUE_WORKTREE and DANGERESQUE_ARTIFACT are deliberately absent here — neither exists yet at dispatch time.
_doc_dispatchGate_workOrderPattern: Optional regex naming the issue comment that carries the spec being dispatched (a project convention — dangeresque knows no comment format). Set it and requireInvestigateBeforeImplement stops asking 'has this issue EVER had an INVESTIGATE' and starts asking 'did one run AFTER the current spec was written', comparing the newest -INVESTIGATE.md artifact's start time against the newest matching comment's createdAt. Without it, the first INVESTIGATE ever archived satisfies the gate forever, including for scope invented weeks later. Matched with the `m` flag. Absent, or matching no comment (including an issue with no comments), keeps the existence-only check — a project opts into strictness by writing down the convention it already follows. An uncompilable regex throws at load time. Minimized comments and comments with no createdAt are ignored. --force bypasses, as with the rest of this policy.
_doc_mergeGate: Pre-merge enforcement gate. Runs BEFORE `git merge` inside mergeWorktree and refuses (exit 2, gateRefusal) if any blocking check fails. Also injects DANGERESQUE_MERGE=1 into the git merge environment so consumer git hooks can distinguish dangeresque merges from direct commits. Absent block = gate off. Commands run in projectRoot with DANGERESQUE_ISSUE + DANGERESQUE_MODE + DANGERESQUE_MERGE=1 + DANGERESQUE_WORKTREE (the merge candidate's checkout — point diff-based checks here, not at projectRoot) + DANGERESQUE_ARTIFACT / DANGERESQUE_ARTIFACT_JSON (the run report being merged and its eval JSON) env vars.
_doc_other_examples: Cargo project: { name: 'compile', cmd: 'cargo build', on_failure: 'block' }, { name: 'test', cmd: 'cargo test', on_failure: 'block' }
Go project:    { name: 'vet', cmd: 'go vet ./...', on_failure: 'block' }, { name: 'test', cmd: 'go test ./...', on_failure: 'block' }
TypeScript-only type check: { name: 'typecheck', cmd: 'tsc --noEmit', on_failure: 'block' }
Operator escape hatch: pass --no-verify to skip for one run; or set verify.enabled=false in config; or drop the offending command from `commands`.
